title: Optimization Terminal Discrimination Record
description: runs/iter-N/confirmation.json (design spec 3.3, 3.5) -- the record of ONE round of TERMINAL DISCRIMINATION. The paper's Figure 1 names this state `discriminate`; this branch calls it `confirm`, and the behaviour here is the paper's: a shortlist S subset of X_valid is measured FRESHLY and its members are compared against each other, so the final comparison does not rest on the fitted response at all. Written by orchestrator.optimize.stage_runner._finish_confirm. shortlist.json is written next to it as a POINTER to this file (see shortlist.schema.json) so the finalists and their measurements have exactly one source of truth. This is the assumption-light half of the two-bound obligation: residual_regret_terminal lives here at delta_terminal, residual_regret_model lives in recommendation.json at delta_screen, and no artifact carries a combined number.

stage.description: The terminal-discrimination state's name in this branch. Constant because no other state writes this artifact.

iteration.description: The iteration index this round ran at. The terminal state can SELF-LOOP, so successive rounds land in successive iterations.

round.description: Which terminal round this is. Round r > 1 keeps the previous winner plus every challenger whose bound still exceeded epsilon -- exactly those that could still change the epsilon-optimal decision. The registered round cap and the budget guard are what terminate the loop; the interpreter never decides it.

finalists.description: The REALIZED shortlist and its fresh measurements, one entry per finalist that was scheduled.

key.description: Stable per-round finalist handle (f0, f1, ...). `bounds` and `terminal_bound.challenger` reference finalists by this key rather than repeating their levels.

why.description: Which rung of the seeding ladder seated this finalist -- the model's answer, the best measured valid configuration, a model top candidate, a round-r carry-over, or known_valid_baseline. Recorded so a reader can tell what the shortlist was PUTTING ON TRIAL from what it was TRUSTING.

samples.description: This finalist's usable fresh replicate values. Empty when every replicate was excluded.

means.description: Multi-objective campaigns only: this finalist's mean over its usable replicates, per objective metric (`mean` stays the first objective's, for single-objective consumers). null for an objective with no usable replicate.

status.description: Why this finalist left the running, not merely that it did. MEASURED INVALIDITY TRUMPS PREDICTION: a single measured violation excludes the finalist outright rather than being averaged away over its surviving replicates, because a configuration that is admissible only sometimes is not admissible. `infeasible` means a replicate was measured inadmissible (or rejected) -- real information about the design space, and the configuration should be struck off. `unmeasured` means the instrument could not measure an ADMISSIBLE configuration (timeout, crash, unparseable output) -- a re-run with a larger budget may recover it, and striking it off would be wrong. The two were one value (`excluded`) until a timed-out finalist was reported as though it had violated a constraint.

best.description: The winning finalist's `key`, or null when no finalist produced a valid measurement at all (which is a real outcome, not an error -- the report ladder then falls to `baseline` or `none`).

bounds.description: PER-CHALLENGER upper bounds against the winner alone, keyed by finalist key, each computed at delta_terminal with M=1. That is the right level for a `keep measuring this one?` screening decision and the WRONG level for a certificate -- the certified verdict reads terminal_bound.value (the simultaneous max) and never these. Round r+1 reads this to decide who is still in contention.

epsilon.description: The resolved epsilon-optimality tolerance residual_regret_terminal is compared against: the declared `pct` of the reference named by epsilon_reference (or the declared `abs`). Null only when there is no reference at all -- unknown, never 0.

epsilon_reference.description: WHICH reference a percentage epsilon was resolved against. `best_finalist`: the winning admissible finalist's fresh mean (the normal case). `best_observed`: no finalist was admissible, so the best measured ADMISSIBLE configuration so far (per-configuration feasibility; `levels`/`value` name it). `recommendation`: nothing admissible was measured, so the epsilon the fitting stage resolved in recommendation.json. `declared_abs`: an absolute epsilon needs no reference. `none`: nothing to take a percentage of, so epsilon is null (unknown) -- never 0, which can never certify and is not what the author declared.

residual_regret_terminal.description: R_delta(x) from terminal discrimination at delta_terminal (design spec 3.5) -- the simultaneous max over the ADMISSIBLE members of the realized shortlist, carrying nothing but their fresh measurements. Null when no finalist produced a valid measurement, when the bound was not estimable, or when ANY admissible finalist went unmeasured: that rival's U_t is unknown, so the max over the shortlist is unknown, and an unknown is not a zero (INV-SEM02) -- a survivors-only max would UNDERSTATE the regret against exactly the rival nobody measured. The survivors-only number is then recorded as terminal_bound_measured_only. UNAFFECTED by an INADMISSIBLE finalist: that one is outside X_valid, the bound over the admissible shortlist is still valid, and it is `certified` that the exclusion suppresses. Never collapsed with recommendation.json's residual_regret_model, which is a different number at a different delta from disjoint inputs.

terminal_bound.description: The full record behind residual_regret_terminal, including WHICH arithmetic ran. Recorded so a reader can tell which bound they are looking at rather than inferring it from the branch date: pairing that reached only the artifact would leave the campaign reporting the wider bound while claiming the narrower method.

challenger.description: The finalist KEY that attains the bound (a levels dict at the model stage). A key rather than a dict because this file already records every finalist's levels against its key, and two representations of one fact can drift apart.

method.description: bonferroni_one_sided_t_paired when common random numbers were actually shared (design spec 3.8), bonferroni_one_sided_welch_t otherwise. A campaign with no declared workload seed gets Welch deliberately: the paired form stays VALID when the seeds were not shared but loses efficiency, and worse, would record a paired method about an experiment that paired nothing.

certification_withheld.description: Why `certified` is false, as named reasons rather than an unexplained boolean -- so a reader can tell a bound that was simply too wide from a GLOBAL claim withheld because the delta_screen premise was broken, or from a shortlist that was never fully compared. Empty exactly when certified is true. `finalist_measured_infeasible` and `fit_exclusions_level_correlated` are the two premise-breaking reasons: both are evidence that the model's ranking is not tracking the constrained objective, so epsilon-optimality over X_valid is unearned even though residual_regret_terminal (a number over the admissible shortlist resting on fresh measurements and no model) remains valid and is still reported. `finalist_unmeasured` means an admissible finalist produced no usable measurement (timeout, crash, unparseable output): the comparison is incomplete, residual_regret_terminal is null, and the remedy is to re-run it rather than strike it off. `no_admissible_finalist` means EVERY finalist was measured inadmissible (each had at least one replicate violating a declared constraint): the measurements are valid and complete, there is simply no admissible configuration in this shortlist to bound, so it replaces `bound_not_computable` (which means too little data to estimate a bound) and is distinct from a NaN response (an instrumentation defect). `model_inadequate` means the latest fitting stage's lack-of-fit F on pure error rejected the registered response class (recommendation.json model_adequate: false): the shortlist was seeded from measured leaders and the ranking of a rejected surface, so nothing supports the delta_screen premise that screening did not exclude the winner (design spec 3.6 rung 3 sits below certification). The within-shortlist bound is still reported. `lack_of_fit_not_computable`, `curvature_untested` and `curvature_not_isolated` mean the latest fitting stage's model adequacy is UNKNOWN (recommendation.json model_adequate: null, model_adequate_basis names which): the lack-of-fit test could not be computed, a choice level was never measured at the centre, or a mixed fit could not separate curvature from its coefficients. The shortlist is built as for an adequate model, but the global claim is withheld. WP-A A1 (spec 2026-10-17-certification-soundness.md): `model_bound_above_epsilon` -- R_model_outside + R_terminal > epsilon (global_bound), so a configuration screening did not shortlist may still beat the winner by more than epsilon; `model_bound_not_computable` -- no model bound exists (no fitting stage this epoch, or no pure error); `model_bound_not_exhaustive` -- the candidate space was SEARCHED, so R_model is silent about unevaluated candidates; `model_recommendation_not_compared` -- the fitted argmax x_hat was not measured admissibly in this round, so the model bound cannot be linked to the winner; `model_recommendation_infeasible` -- x_hat was measured inadmissible, so the step f(x_hat) <= f(best admissible finalist) fails and nothing links the model bound to the winner. Single-objective only. `baseline_measured_inadmissible` (#321): the declared known_valid_baseline, seated as the permanent reference finalist, had a replicate violating a declared constraint -- the declaration contradicts the measurement, so the certificate is withheld; `finalist_measured_infeasible` then names only OTHER finalists.

global_bound.description: Single-objective only (WP-A A1, spec 2026-10-17-certification-soundness.md section 2): G = R_model_outside + R_terminal, which certification requires to be <= epsilon. R_model_outside is the fitting stage's simultaneous model bound against its argmax x_hat, maxed over the candidates OUTSIDE this round's measured shortlist (delta_screen); R_terminal is this round's terminal bound (delta_terminal_per_look). The sum bounds f(x*) - f(w) through f(x_hat) <= f(best admissible finalist), so x_hat must be measured admissibly this round (x_hat_key). value is null when that link or a model bound is missing; certification_withheld names why.

heteroscedasticity.description: #321 P3 item 1: the Brown-Forsythe check of M3 (the pure error is the variance at every configuration): the one-sided planned contrast 'this round's admissible finalists spread more than the fitting stage's pure-error cells' on the absolute-deviation-from-median scale (structural zeros removed), at the registered alpha; the omnibus F over every group is recorded under omnibus. rejected: true withholds heteroscedastic_pure_error; p null withholds heteroscedasticity_not_testable (reason names why).

gain_over_baseline.description: WP-A A3 (spec 2026-10-17-certification-soundness.md section 5), single-objective campaigns declaring known_valid_baseline: the winner's gain over the baseline, which confirm seats in EVERY round as a permanent reference finalist (outside shortlist_size, sharing the round's workload seeds, so CRN-paired under workload.seed_env). Signed in the campaign's direction (positive = better than the baseline). [low, high] is a two-sided interval at delta, Bonferroni over every finalist vs the baseline, so it covers the data-SELECTED winner's true gain with probability >= 1 - delta (selection-proof). `estimate` is the winner's mean difference on the same replicates that selected it and is biased upward; the interval is the claim. null estimate: the baseline produced no admissible measurement, or no variance estimate.

delta_guaranteed.description: The coverage the interval GUARANTEES as reported: 1 - delta_guaranteed, where delta_guaranteed is the declared delta_terminal. The interval is computed at the per-look level, but the reported round is the one the campaign stopped at, so optional stopping over the registered looks leaves only the union bound.

censored_replicates.description: #321 P3 item 3 (A6): per finalist, the replicates that TIMED OUT -- right-censored at run_timeout_sec (at_sec), with the bound that implies; never imputed. The finalist is unmeasured, so the round withholds finalist_unmeasured.

distributional_feasibility.description: #321 P3 item 3 (A6): constraints declared with semantics mean | chance:<alpha>. Each finalist must be SHOWN feasible from its replicates, per such constraint, at per_test_level = delta_feasibility / (finalists x constraints x looks): a one-sided t bound on the mean, or a one-sided Clopper-Pearson (1934) upper bound on the violation probability <= alpha. A finalist not shown feasible is status infeasible (struck off). delta_feasibility is a term of the stated union bound.

outliers.description: #321 P3 item 3 (A6): confirm replicates flagged by their deleted-residual t within each finalist (own variance, so heteroscedastic finalists do not flag each other), Bonferroni over every tested replicate of the round. FLAG ONLY (deleted: false); sensitivity says whether dropping the flagged replicates would change the winner. Finalists with fewer than 4 replicates are listed under untested.

noise_diagnostics.description: #321 P3 item 2 (A5): per-finalist n, variance and skewness (Fisher g1), the variance ratio (largest over smallest finalist variance), the skewness pretest, the robust family's per-challenger bounds (t and robust: exact sign-flip under CRN, bootstrap-t otherwise) and the named withheld reasons (replicates_below_floor, noise_skewed, robust_bound_not_computable).

allocation.description: WP-D D1 (opt-in design.confirm.allocate): the registered allocate branch's seats for the NEXT round, chosen by allocate.allocate on the fitted model's predictions (knowledge gradient / EHVI per run) and registered here before the transition reads allocate_available. Selection only: no field here enters any bound; a seat's claim rests on its fresh replicates in the allocate round. declined names why nothing was seated (allocate.DECLINE_REASONS, allocate_seat.SEAT_DECLINE_REASONS), null otherwise.

alpha_spending.description: WP-A A2: Bonferroni alpha-spending over the epoch's confirm LOOKS. Every round evaluates `certified` and stops on it, so each round is a look, judged at per_look = delta_terminal_declared / looks with looks = confirm_max_rounds, plus one when the refill branch is registered. delta_terminal in this file is per_look.

certified.description: The GLOBAL epsilon-optimality verdict over X_valid, which rests on Pr(wrong global decision) <= delta_screen + delta_terminal. False whenever ANY finalist was measured inadmissible, even if the within-shortlist bound came in at or below epsilon: an inadmissible finalist is direct evidence that the model's ranking is not tracking the CONSTRAINED objective, so the delta_screen premise (screening did not exclude the true optimum) does not hold and the sum bound is unearned. The within-shortlist number stays reported; only the global label is withheld.

pareto.description: Multi-objective campaigns only (spec 2026-10-15-pareto-front-design.md steps 5-8): the MEASURED front over every admissible configuration the campaign measured (confirm finalists and fitting-stage rows, means over complete rows), each point's dominance status, the preferred point, the hypervolume and the remaining gaps.

front.description: Points no other measured point eps-dominates in point estimate, sorted best-first by the first objective. `confidently_nondominated`: for EVERY other measured point some objective's one-sided upper bound on its advantage is below that objective's epsilon (pooled pure-error variance, Bonferroni over rivals x objectives at delta_front), and no adequate-model prediction beats it by epsilon on every objective. Otherwise `possibly_dominated`, and `dominated_by` names who could not be ruled out.

value.description: null (with `reason`) when no point is confidently_nondominated: undefined, not zero.

gap_threshold.description: null when no objective's epsilon is known: no gap can be called large.

epsilon_unknown.description: Objectives whose epsilon has no reference (null in `epsilon`); certification is withheld (epsilon_unknown).

predicted_rivals.description: Whether predicted-front candidates were checked as rivals of measured points (only when every objective model is adequate).

dropped.description: true: no usable row remains on some objective, so the configuration is left out of the front (a confirm finalist among these is unmeasured and blocks certification). false: only some rows were unusable; the configuration is measured on its usable rows.

excluded_incomplete.description: Measured admissible configurations with a complete row that lacked a usable value for some objective (missing, null, NaN or non-numeric). See `dropped` for whether the configuration itself left the front.

certification_caveats.description: Facts that weaken the certificate's premise without withholding it. Present only when non-empty. `finalist_measured_infeasible`: a finalist was measured inadmissible but at least two admissible finalists remained, their simultaneous bound is within epsilon and the model was adequate (stage_runner._INFEASIBLE_FINALIST_CAVEAT).

warnings.description: Inputs this round could not read or use (a missing or corrupt refill_pool.json, an uncodeable level), each also logged at WARNING. Present only when non-empty.

paired.description: Whether replicate i of every finalist actually ran the same workload seed (common random numbers, design spec 3.8), set from the campaign's declared optimization.workload.seed_env. Forwarded to the bound computation, not merely recorded: the paired form works on DIFFERENCES so the workload's contribution cancels and the bound shrinks substantially.

delta_terminal.description: The PER-LOOK terminal risk this file's bound is stated at (WP-A A2: the compiled policy's delta_terminal divided by the epoch's registered confirm looks; see alpha_spending), kept distinct from delta_screen throughout.

excluded_infeasible.description: The levels of every finalist measured INADMISSIBLE (or rejected). Non-empty is what withholds `certified` above, so it is recorded rather than derived. The name predates the infeasible/unmeasured split and is kept for existing readers; it now contains only genuinely inadmissible finalists.

excluded_unmeasured.description: The levels of every finalist whose MEASUREMENT failed -- timeout, crash, unparseable output -- rather than being inadmissible. Also withholds `certified`, because the terminal comparison has no fresh samples for it either, but it carries the opposite authoring consequence from `excluded_infeasible`: re-run with a larger budget rather than strike the configuration off.

confirmed_at_levels.description: The WINNING finalist's levels. A legacy single-point field kept because readers of it exist (the harness's recommendation fallback, the guide's worked output, the report ladder's terminal rungs); it now names the winner rather than the only configuration run. Empty when there is no winner.

replicates.description: Total replicate runs scheduled this round, across all finalists.

usable_replicates.description: How many of those produced a usable measurement. The gap between this and `replicates` is what an exclusion looks like in aggregate.

mean.description: The winner's mean over its fresh replicates -- a MEASUREMENT, unlike recommendation.json's `predicted`. Null when there is no winner.

spread.description: Population standard deviation of the winner's replicates; 0.0 with fewer than two of them.

observations.description: The winner's individual replicate values, so the mean and spread above are auditable rather than asserted. Empty when there is no winner.

best_observed.description: OPTIONAL and present only when there is both a winner and a best measured valid configuration to compare it against. Two keys: `levels`, and the campaign's own PRIMARY METRIC NAME carrying that configuration's value -- so the second key is campaign-dependent and cannot be enumerated here, which is why this object stays open. `the best finalist` and `the best configuration found` are different claims, and recording both keeps the artifact honest when they disagree -- a mis-specified surface can leave the winner below a corner an earlier state measured.

confirmed_is_best_observed.description: OPTIONAL, written alongside best_observed: whether the winner actually matched or beat it.

regression_vs_best_observed.description: OPTIONAL, written ONLY when confirmed_is_best_observed is false -- the size of the shortfall. Its presence is the signal that the observed corner, not the winner, is the campaign's real answer and the surface is mis-specified -- UNLESS within_epsilon is true: a single earlier row is an upward-biased estimate of its configuration, and a gap inside the campaign's own indifference width is recorded rather than raised. Never written when the best observed row belongs to the winning configuration itself.

terminal_bound_measured_only.description: PRESENT ONLY when a finalist went unmeasured while the measured finalists still yielded a bound: that bound, over the measured finalists alone. Recorded because the comparison among the survivors genuinely happened; NOT residual_regret_terminal, because it is silent about the unmeasured rival(s) and would understate the regret.
